paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God doesn't just make promises, He backs them up. Abram asked God two honest questions, one about an heir and one about the land. God never scolded him for asking. He answered both, and He answered them with stars and with a covenant.

Now look at what Abram did with that sky full of stars. Genesis 15:6 says, "Abram believed the LORD, and it was credited to him as righteousness." He had no child yet, and he believed anyway. He didn't earn it by doing something big. He trusted the One who made the promise, and God counted that trust as righteousness.

Then comes the part where I lean in close. In Genesis 15:17, a smoking firepot and a flaming torch pass between the halves, and Abram was asleep for it (Genesis 15:12). I think that means the promise didn't hang on Abram holding up his end, it hung on God. So here's what it means for you, baker: when you're waiting on God and the answer looks impossible, you can lean your whole weight on His word, because He is the One who keeps it.
